messages:
alex: noticed a weird pattern in eu-west3 this morning — batch GPU jobs are waiting on local ssd IO and some pods hit Read-only after a cleanup run

maria: saw the same, GPU provisioning queue spiked around 07:12 UTC and nvme io went to 95% for ~3m

jordan: any errors in node logs? could be scrub / janitor overlap

alex: logs show scrub started then a bunch of stale-evict ops queued, then kernel reprobes, sample log: 
```
Aug 12 07:11:58 node-eu3 kubelet[2345]: scrubber[pid=4123]: scan start /dev/nvme0n1p1
Aug 12 07:12:03 node-eu3 kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
Aug 12 07:12:05 node-eu3 local-cleaner[1987]: mark readonly /var/lib/kubelet/pods/...
Aug 12 07:12:18 node-eu3 kube-provisioner: pod wait backoff: insufficient local storage
```

devon: hmm blk_update_request + readonly usually firmware or bad remap table, but the timing with scrub is suspicious

maria: scrub schedule is staggered, but yesterday we pushed a scrub config change (reduce parallelism) to eu-west3-canaries. Could that have made cleaners overlap?

alex: config change: `SCRUB_PARALLEL=8 -> 4` at 02:00 UTC. The controller tried to compensate by scheduling more frequent small runs; looks like two janitor sets collided on same host during a heavy embedding job window

jordan: embedding jobs have long sequences, they hit writeback pressure and inflate IO queue depth. If scrub and janitor both do metadata reads/writes it pushes async remap into timeout and nvme returns read errors -> kernel marks device flaky -> readonly

ops-lead: immediate ask: is it safe to revert the scrub scheduler to yesterday's rollout? what mitigations to bring nodes back to healthy without data loss

devon: short term: cordon affected nodes, avoid scheduling GPU bursts there, run `fsck -y` in maintenance (we have copies for ephemeral scratch but still run checks). For nodes in readonly, remount read-only, `dmesg` indicates remap failures, we should drain GPU pools for those hosts

alex: plan: 1) stop janitor on eu-west3 canaries 2) pause scrub controller 3) drain 6 affected nodes 4) run nvme-cli smart-log + fwrollback if SMART shows anomalies 5) re-provision with fresh local-ssd images if RW not recoverable

maria: adding cost note — re-provisioning ~6 hosts = ~0.9k hourly burn for replacement GPUs while seeding new instances, but keeps SLOs. prefer to avoid full reprovision if fw fix works

jordan: command snippets: 
```
# check nvme
nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1
# assess kernel retries
grep -i "blk_update_request" /var/log/kern.log | tail -n 50
# force fsck safely
umount /var/lib/kubelet && fsck.ext4 -fy /dev/nvme0n1p1
```

devon: also add a temporary admission webhook to limit local-ssd-intensive jobs in eu-west3 for next 2 hours (batch -> no local write). That buys time for investigation

ops-lead: agreed. Maria, please coordinate rollback of scrub change and stop janitor. Alex + Devon, start node drains and fsck triage. Jordan, collect kernel+nvme logs and post summary in this thread

maria: stopping janitor now on canaries. rolling back SCRUB_PARALLEL to 8. patch queued to rollback controller, will promote in 3m

alex: draining nodes 7->12, starting one at a time. first node shows SMART: Critical Warning: 0x01 (trim errors) and media errors count increasing

jordan: collected logs attached to s3://redwood-debug/eu-west3/3532109876.tar.gz (permission: infra-read). snippets: majority show elevated write latency + remap_count growth

devon: onboarding webhook to limit local-ssd writes pushed (policy id: policy-eu3-ld). Should reduce new pressure immediately

maria: rollback promoted. scrub controller reports cadence restored to previous spacing. Janitor stopped on canaries

ops-lead: status update in 20m. If any node still RW-fails after fsck, we replace and mark serial for vendor RMA depending on SMART thresholds

alex: quick note — found two nodes where ephemeral cleanup truncated a write during GC and left a partial metadata object; that's likely root cause for the corruption flags. We'll add an extra pre-check to janitor to avoid concurrent GC on live GPU hosts

jordan: filing follow-up infra task: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-3897 — title: "janitor: preflight lock to avoid concurrent metadata GC on same device"

devon: also propose a gradual scrub ramp algorithm (windowed stagger + backoff when I/O saturates) — will draft RFC

ops-lead: good. capture cost/impact in INFRA-3897. Thanks team.

alex: will post final remediation summary once all nodes either recovered or reprovisioned. :thumbsup:
